amends: r6-geometry-contract-02 tessellation rule, for a NEW candidate R6-b only; R6-a is completed and judged under 02/02a/02b unchanged
authored: 2026-11-16 KST, orchestrator (Opus), before the R6-b STL exists
trigger: worker sonnet-r6-gen calibration: on a development R6 fuselage, surfaceCheck v1912 reports 1290 locations while the locator reports 0 and no non-adjacent triangle lies within one cell of any hit; 99.9 % of hits sit at vertices with an exactly axis-parallel edge (x-parallel longitudinal edges in the prismatic mid-body, y-parallel ring edges on flat belly/crown clips). Synthetic open cylinder 32x100: 2497 locations; half-cell ring stagger -> 0; 1e-5 y or z jitter -> 0 (x-only jitter does not help); a 'leaning' strip triangulation with no ring-to-ring edge parallel to an axis -> 0. Interpretation: a checker response to exactly axis-parallel edges, not a geometric intersection.

change.tessellation: between adjacent rings/sections use a leaning strip triangulation in which no ring-to-ring (longitudinal or spanwise) edge is exactly parallel to a coordinate axis; every ledger point stays a vertex; no jitter or coordinate perturbation of any vertex is allowed
change.unchanged: all gates G1-G7 and A1-A4, every 02a threshold (including min angle, aspect, grading, valence, dihedral, kink), three-checker self-intersection 0 with surfaceCheck still a gate, 02b clarifications

reporting.r6_a: R6-a (literal 02 tessellation) is kept and reported with its G3 surfaceCheck result and the calibration evidence; it is not regraded
reporting.r6_b: if R6-b still shows surfaceCheck records (for example on y-parallel ring edges of the flat belly/crown clips that come from fixed ledger points), M3 stays FAIL and the records are reported with their edge-orientation analysis

side_finding: the R3 ledger fuselage has exactly flat crown and belly clips (C15 records at z = 6.09 m and 1.95 m); the real A321 cross-section is not flat there. This is recorded as a geometry-source defect to address in a later candidate, not in R6-b.
